title: Fridge Politics
logline: Midnight in the house: wherever things of one kind live, they hold an election. The loud rival promises more of the old flaw, the wholesome one sounds nice, and the quiet candidate is {{product.name}}. Then a real voter opens the door.

ingested: the fridge election is fully rendered (rivals, moderator, audience, venue) and bottles, pouches or snacks slot straight in; the cap or tab is a natural mouth
applied: the bathroom-cabinet election; tubes, pumps, jars and droppers all have a cap or nozzle for a mouth; rival and venue cards must be generated per product
worn: the hall-closet election; shoes and garments talk through their collar opening, glasses and watches with hops; rival and venue cards must be generated per product
handheld: the junk-drawer election; cases and gadgets talk through a lid or hinge, screens and lenses stay clean; rival and venue cards must be generated per product
carried: the coat-hook election; a zip is the most natural mouth there is and bags hang like candidates at podiums; rival and venue cards must be generated per product
home: the living-room election at real room scale; lamps, speakers, pillows and chairs work, but room-scale objects are harder to animate and she must sit on or switch on the product rather than pick it up
consumable: the pantry election; box flaps and tear strips make easy mouths; rival and venue cards must be generated per product

avoid: products whose front is a screen or print that would have to carry the face
comparisons that name or visually echo a real competitor

lore: The house belongs to Marisol Vega, a small place in San Antonio where almost everything was bought second-hand in 2014; the fridge door seal is so tired that frost builds on the back wall.

Every night at midnight, wherever things of one kind live in this house (shelf two of the fridge, the bathroom cabinet, the hall closet, the junk drawer, the coat hooks, the living room, the pantry), they hold an election. Whoever the voter picks goes with her; everyone else waits another night.
Buck has won nine elections in a row, mostly on weekends, and has never once been picked for a work night.
The audience is always one short: an egg went into this morning's omelette, a cotton bud or a sock went missing. The empty spot sits in the front row.
Marisol starts a twelve-hour night shift at 12:30am at the fictional St. Aldric Hospital. Whoever she picks tonight goes with her until dawn.
world_bible.materials_rule: Everything is a real household object shot as photoreal macro product photography (at real room scale in the living room); the only stylization is the faces (glossy animated eyes and mouths that sit on the object's surface and catch the same light) and the rivals' thin noodle arms. Debate furniture is improvised from the venue's own odds and ends: bottle caps, jar lids, shoebox lids, takeout lids, coat hooks, coasters, crinkled foil, toothpicks, rubber bands, twist ties. Faces exist only on the named characters and the audience in the shots where they act: location plates and prop sheets show plain objects with no eyes. Every surface carries real wear: condensation, frost, dust, smears and crumbs.

world_bible.venue_rule: This template runs in a different venue per product.archetype, so the product lives among its own kind. Before filling, replace every bracketed venue token in shots and units, [venue], [night light], [warm light], [opening], [podium], [audience], [pov] and [entrance], with the values in venues.<product.archetype>; use that venue's plate as the location reference and its Buck, Brenda and Pat cards as the rival and moderator references. Rivals are always generic, unbranded members of the product's own category and never a real competitor's shape, colour or trade dress: Buck is always the loud old-school version in purple with one gold star, Brenda always the wholesome-sounding version in orange with a simple orange-slice mark. If the product's exact kind differs from the defaults (a serum instead of a cream, a hoodie instead of a sneaker), recast the two rivals as the same kind as the product, keeping their colours, marks, faces and voices. No bracket may remain after filling.

Native sound: the venue's hum, a light click, audience murmurs. No music. No text, labels blank except the product.

Its label and front never move, bend or grow a face; only its eyes and its existing opening move. Shot 2 (3.8 to 6 s): @Image2 (Buck) tilts back in a scoffing belly laugh: "Ha! Nobody picks the quiet one." Keep the product's shape, colours and label exactly as @Image1. Native sound: the venue's hum, one gasp from the audience, the laugh. No music.

9:16 photoreal. Shot 1 (0 to 1.6 s): [opening], [warm light] floods the venue and every object freezes like an ordinary object, faces neutral and still; {{action.S07}}. Shot 2 (1.6 to 4.4 s): low POV [pov]: @Image1 (Marisol, a tired nurse in navy scrubs) looks in, rubs her eye, to herself: "{{line.L6}}" Shot 3 (4.4 to 7.6 s): {{action.S09}}, past the frozen @Image2 (Buck) and @Image3 (Brenda); the product matches @Image6 exactly, undistorted. Shot 4 (7.6 to 11 s): the venue closes, dark, the night light clicks back on; [audience] erupt cheering, @Image4 (Pat) flips up like a thrown hat: "The people have spoken!" Buck turns to Brenda, deflated: "Recount?" Objects only move while the venue is closed. Native sound: the opening, house room tone, a clink or creak, the closing, cheering. No music. No text.

Slow push-in, camera 10 to 20 degrees above the top edge, on {{action.S11}}; the product matches @Image1 exactly and does not move, bend or grow a face on its label. Clean dark space above it. music.brief: Mock election fanfare: snare roll and pompous brass in B flat, 108 bpm, a little honky and small like a school band, ducking under each line.
The brass drops out; a cool muted vibraphone and upright bass groove under the product's line, then a tuba raspberry on Buck's laugh.
Hard stop to silence on the opening (the freeze), a single held high string note while she chooses, then the full fanfare explodes as the venue closes and a sad trombone for the recount.
The vibraphone groove returns, resolves on one warm chord under the tagline.
